ESV.1: There was a man of the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Micah.
ESV.2: And he said to his mother, “The 1,100 pieces of silver that were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse, and also spoke it in my ears, behold, the silver is with me; I took it.” And his mother said, “Blessed be my son by the LORD.”
ESV.3: And he restored the 1,100 pieces of silver to his mother. And his mother said, “I dedicate the silver to the LORD from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a metal image. Now therefore I will restore it to you.”
ESV.4: So when he restored the money to his mother, his mother took 200 pieces of silver and gave it to the silversmith, who made it into a carved image and a metal image. And it was in the house of Micah.
ESV.5: And the man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and household gods, and ordained  one of his sons, who became his priest.
ESV.6: In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
ESV.7: Now there was a young man of Bethlehem in Judah, of the family of Judah, who was a Levite, and he sojourned there.
ESV.8: And the man departed from the town of Bethlehem in Judah to sojourn where he could find a place. And as he journeyed, he came to the hill country of Ephraim to the house of Micah.
ESV.9: And Micah said to him, “Where do you come from?” And he said to him, “I am a Levite of Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to sojourn where I may find a place.”
ESV.10: And Micah said to him, “Stay with me, and be to me a father and a priest, and I will give you ten pieces of silver a year and a suit of clothes and your living.” And the Levite went in.
ESV.11: And the Levite was content to dwell with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.
ESV.12: And Micah ordained the Levite, and the young man became his priest, and was in the house of Micah.
ESV.13: Then Micah said, “Now I know that the LORD will prosper me, because I have a Levite as priest.”

NASB.1: Now there was a man of the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Micah.
NASB.2: He said to his mother, 'The eleven hundred [pieces] of silver which were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse in my hearing, behold, the silver is with me; I took it.' And his mother said, 'Blessed be my son by the LORD.'
NASB.3: He then returned the eleven hundred [pieces] of silver to his mother, and his mother said, 'I wholly dedicate the silver from my hand to the LORD for my son to make a graven image and a molten image; now therefore, I will return them to you.'
NASB.4: So when he returned the silver to his mother, his mother took two hundred [pieces] of silver and gave them to the silversmith who made them into a graven image and a molten image, and they were in the house of Micah.
NASB.5: And the man Micah had a shrine and he made an ephod and household idols and consecrated one of his sons, that he might become his priest.
NASB.6: In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did what was right in his own eyes.
NASB.7: Now there was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, of the family of Judah, who was a Levite; and he was staying there.
NASB.8: Then the man departed from the city, from Bethlehem in Judah, to stay wherever he might find [a place]; and as he made his journey, he came to the hill country of Ephraim to the house of Micah.
NASB.9: Micah said to him, 'Where do you come from?' And he said to him, 'I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to stay wherever I may find [a place].'
NASB.10: Micah then said to him, 'Dwell with me and be a father and a priest to me, and I will give you ten [pieces] of silver a year, a suit of clothes, and your maintenance.' So the Levite went [in].
NASB.11: The Levite agreed to live with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.
NASB.12: So Micah consecrated the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in the house of Micah.
NASB.13: Then Micah said, 'Now I know that the LORD will prosper me, seeing I have a Levite as priest.'

NLT.1: There was a man named Micah, who lived in the hill country of Ephraim.
NLT.2: One day he said to his mother, “I heard you place a curse on the person who stole 1,100 pieces of silver from you. Well, I have the money. I was the one who took it.” “The LORD bless you for admitting it,” his mother replied.
NLT.3: He returned the money to her, and she said, “I now dedicate these silver coins to the LORD. In honor of my son, I will have an image carved and an idol cast.”
NLT.4: So when he returned the money to his mother, she took 200 silver coins and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into an image and an idol. And these were placed in Micah’s house.
NLT.5: Micah set up a shrine for the idol, and he made a sacred ephod and some household idols. Then he installed one of his sons as his personal priest.
NLT.6: In those days Israel had no king; all the people did whatever seemed right in their own eyes.
NLT.7: One day a young Levite, who had been living in Bethlehem in Judah, arrived in that area.
NLT.8: He had left Bethlehem in search of another place to live, and as he traveled, he came to the hill country of Ephraim. He happened to stop at Micah’s house as he was traveling through.
NLT.9: “Where are you from?” Micah asked him. He replied, “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am looking for a place to live.”
NLT.10: “Stay here with me,” Micah said, “and you can be a father and priest to me. I will give you ten pieces of silver a year, plus a change of clothes and your food.”
NLT.11: The Levite agreed to this, and the young man became like one of Micah’s sons.
NLT.12: So Micah installed the Levite as his personal priest, and he lived in Micah’s house.
NLT.13: “I know the LORD will bless me now,” Micah said, “because I have a Levite serving as my priest.”

NET.1: There was a man named Micah from the Ephraimite hill country.
NET.2: He said to his mother, “You know the eleven hundred pieces of silver which were stolen from you, about which I heard you pronounce a curse? Look here, I have the silver. I stole it, but now I am giving it back to you.” His mother said, “May the LORD reward you, my son!”
NET.3: When he gave back to his mother the eleven hundred pieces of silver, his mother said, “I solemnly dedicate this silver to the LORD. It will be for my son’s benefit. We will use it to make a carved image and a metal image.”
NET.4: When he gave the silver back to his mother, she took two hundred pieces of silver to a silversmith, who made them into a carved image and a metal image. She then put them in Micah’s house.
NET.5: Now this man Micah owned a shrine. He made an ephod and some personal idols and hired one of his sons to serve as a priest.
NET.6: In those days Israel had no king. Each man did what he considered to be right.
NET.7: There was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah. He was a Levite who had been temporarily residing among the tribe of Judah.
NET.8: This man left the town of Bethlehem in Judah to find another place to live. He came to the Ephraimite hill country and made his way to Micah’s house.
NET.9: Micah said to him, “Where do you come from?” He replied, “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah. I am looking for a new place to live.”
NET.10: Micah said to him, “Stay with me. Become my adviser and priest. I will give you ten pieces of silver per year, plus clothes and food.”
NET.11: So the Levite agreed to stay with the man; the young man was like a son to Micah.
NET.12: Micah paid the Levite; the young man became his priest and lived in Micah’s house.
NET.13: Micah said, “Now I know God will make me rich, because I have this Levite as my priest.”
